issues.description: Both PageFlags::RW implementations map specification calls to X_spec, so proofs observe execute-only bits 4 instead of the executable read/write bits 3.
issues.rationale: At the selected problem snapshot, both RW bodies and their RW_spec functions compute R|W = 0b001|0b010 = 3, but #[verifier::when_used_as_spec(X_spec)] redirects a specification call to X_spec = 0b100 = 4. The first repair commit replaces the exec/rw copy with an exact allow_in_spec return expression; the final repair commit does the same for the mm copy. The identical copied annotation error is one root with two locations.
issues.source_evidence:
after/lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/pte/page_prop.rs:260-272
RW_spec returns Self { bits: R().bits() | W().bits() }, but RW is annotated #[verifier::when_used_as_spec(X_spec)].

after/lock-protocol/src/mm/page_prop.rs:253-265
The second PageFlags copy repeats the same RW_spec=R|W and when_used_as_spec(X_spec) mismatch.

repair/lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/pte/page_prop.rs @ a8491dff31e06a219b0c4be65771cdc7fee7de72
RW becomes allow_in_spec with an exact return of R().bits() | W().bits().

repair/lock-protocol/src/mm/page_prop.rs @ 58149432cd448cd6c116e581461d3379c4e2c73b
The remaining copy becomes allow_in_spec with the same exact R|W return.
issues.verification: Source review and a Verus 0b6f3cbb/Rust 1.88/Z3 4.12.5 micro-harness: 5 verified, 0 errors; the bad form proves RW().bits == 4 and != 3, while the repaired form proves == 3. Full target: problem 494 verified/0 errors and final 496/0 errors; these passes do not expose a trusted when_used_as_spec redirection. The verifier revision postdates the PR and is compatibility evidence only.
